probeEvidence.notes: Monkey-patched Element.prototype.animate to log every animation. All animations are WAAPI, easing on every call is literally cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1), durations 300 enter / 260 change / 220 leave — all in band, zero CSS class-restart animation, zero linear tweens. Transform retargeting is REAL: interrupted a leave at t=201ms and the new keyframe[0] was matrix(0.94005,0,0,0.94005,-225.811,35.9699), byte-identical to the sampled live pose at t=200ms — no snap-back, no restart. Reduced motion collapses to two 1ms opacity-only keyframes, verified by log. Text scale 200% reflows the entire card (not a preview) and still fits 600x600; 310% scrolls cleanly. BUT: frame-by-frame height trace of an interrupted expand (click at t=0, counter-click at t=112) shows heights 172.5 -> 225.6 (at interrupt) -> continues climbing 228.3, 230, 231.2, 232, 232.6, 233, 233.3, 233.5, 233.6, 233.7 -> then INSTANT jump to 172.5 at t=270. No new height animation was ever created on interrupt; only the detail opacity retarget fired. That is a 61px hard snap on the primary gesture. Separately, .msg:hover{transform:translateY(-2px)} never renders — measured transform stays matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0) under a real mouse hover because the enter animation holds fill:'both'. Separately, two dismisses 200ms apart consumed Maya AND Dad, left 2 [data-card] nodes in the DOM at once, and the queue jumped straight to 'Last one' — a message was silently skipped.

blind.A: visionOS incoming-notification banner (visionOS 2, glass capsule in front of the user, gaze-to-expand into the Messages sheet)
blind.B: Horizon OS Quest notification toast (Quest v60+, dark card sliding up above the app dock / Universal Menu panel)

blindDescriptions.A: A small rounded glass capsule floating a fixed distance in front of the wearer, slightly below and forward of the horizon line. App icon at left, app name in small secondary grey, sender in semibold white, one truncated line of message body. The slab is genuinely refractive: the environment behind it is blurred and displaced, a bright specular hairline runs along the top edge, and a soft contact shadow grounds it in depth. It arrives by translating toward the viewer in Z while fading and unblurring over roughly 400ms on a spring; resting gaze on it expands it into a full conversation sheet, and looking away shrinks it back out. No designed empty/error/offline variant exists for this surface at all — failures fall back into the host app's generic red 'Not Delivered'. Permission grants are a long, wordy system modal.
blindDescriptions.B: A near-opaque dark charcoal rounded rectangle that slides up from below and parks just above the app dock at the bottom of the flat 2D panel. Circular app icon at left, white semibold title, grey body line, dismiss X at right. It stacks vertically when several arrive and the stack reflows with a visible snap. Because the card is essentially opaque there is no sense of the passthrough or environment existing behind it — it reads as an Android notification pasted onto a floating rectangle. Motion is a slide-plus-fade in the low 300s on a stock material ease. It does ship real designed offline and empty-panel screens and honest permission modals, which is more than A does. Nothing about it is memorable.
blindDescriptions.C: A single translucent card parked in the lower third of a 600x600 square, deliberately keeping the centre of view clear world. Backdrop blur 24px with saturation lift, a linear gradient scrim, a one-pixel inset specular highlight along the top edge, and a deep drop shadow — the warm ground and cool sky of the street behind it read clearly through the glass. Three type sizes exactly: sender at 14/600 in 60% ink, timestamp at 11 pushed to the right margin, and the message itself at 22/600 with negative tracking in full white. Two pill actions below. Underneath, at 42% opacity, a three-dot progress trail and '2 more waiting'. Cards leave upward when sent and downward when dismissed, so the direction of the exit encodes the outcome. All five edge states are individually designed with their own glyph, headline, one human sentence and a recovery button; loading is a determinate bar with a real explanation rather than a spinner. Under the hood the transforms are genuinely retargetable mid-flight, but the card's own grow/shrink is not — interrupt the expand and it inflates all the way then snaps 61px shut in one frame.

referenceScreens.visionOS: visionOS 2 incoming-notification banner, the glass capsule that appears in front of you when a Message arrives while you are in the Home View. It is a small rounded slab of true refractive glass — the environment behind it is blurred and slightly displaced, with a bright specular hairline along the top edge and a soft contact shadow — carrying app icon, app name, sender in semibold, and one line of body; holding gaze on it expands it in place into the full Messages sheet, and looking away lets it recede and fade.
referenceScreens.horizonOS: Horizon OS (Quest v60+) notification toast above the app dock. A near-opaque charcoal rounded rectangle slides up from below the panel, with a circular app icon at left, white semibold title and grey body line and a dismiss X at right; multiple toasts stack vertically and the stack reflows with a visible snap, and because the card is opaque the passthrough behind it is completely occluded.

biggestGap: Card expand/collapse height animation is not interruptible — resize() at components/16-motion/index.html:198-206 measures h1 on line 201 AFTER mutate() but BEFORE cancelling the in-flight height animation, so while an expand is running the still-active animation forces the measured height and h1 minus h0 is under 1px, the guard on line 202 returns early, and NO new height animation is ever created. Measured frame trace: expand at t=0 (172.5px -> 233.7px, 260ms), counter-click at t=112ms with card at 225.6px; height then CONTINUES to climb 228.3 / 230 / 231.2 / 232 / 232.6 / 233 / 233.7 and INSTANTLY drops to 172.5px at t=270ms. Expected: the counter-click retargets from the live 225.6px to 172.5px over 260ms on cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1) with zero discontinuity. Got: the interruption is ignored, then a 61px single-frame snap. Fix by cancelling the running height animation and reading its live value into h0 BEFORE mutate(), then measuring h1 with the animation already gone — i.e. h0 = getBoundingClientRect().height; cancel height anims; mutate(); h1 = getBoundingClientRect().height. Note the lab's own 'Interrupt mid-flight' button routes through advance() (transform retarget, which does work) and therefore never demonstrates the path that breaks.
reason: I drove the motion myself rather than trusting a still frame. Half of the motion system is genuinely built and measurably excellent: every animation goes through the Web Animations API (verified by monkey-patching Element.prototype.animate and logging every call), every easing string is literally cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1), durations are 300/260/220 — all inside the 200-320ms band with no linear tweens and no bounce, reduced motion collapses to 1ms opacity-only keyframes, and transform retargeting is frame-accurate: interrupting a leave at t=201ms produced a keyframe starting at matrix(0.94005,0,0,0.94005,-225.811,35.9699), identical to the sampled live pose one frame earlier. That is real, not asserted. But the other half is depicted. The card's own grow/shrink — the most-used gesture on the only focal element — cannot be interrupted at all: the frame trace shows the expand run to completion after the interrupt and then a 61px single-frame snap. On a piece whose entire subject is a motion language, the primary interruption path snapping is disqualifying for the motion criterion. Two further measured defects compound it: .msg:hover{transform:translateY(-2px)} at index.html:42 never renders because the enter animation holds fill:'both', so the authored gaze-hover feedback on the focal card is dead (measured transform stays identity under a real hover); and advance() at index.html:399 selects surface.querySelector('[data-card]'), which still matches the .leaving card, so two dismisses 200ms apart consumed both Maya and Dad, left two cards in the DOM simultaneously, and jumped the queue to 'Last one' — a message is silently lost with no undo, which is a content dead end. Everything else is strong and genuinely beats both references: three type sizes exactly with zero engineering tokens on screen, all five edge states individually designed with a glyph, a headline, one human sentence and a real recovery route (visionOS ships none of these for its notification banner and its loading is a bare spinner), honest glass with a visible warm ground bleeding through, and a text-scale slider that reflows the whole surface at 200% and still fits the stage. Ours ties visionOS at 73 and beats Horizon OS by 21.
passCondition: Ours did NOT rank first outright — it tied first with visionOS at 73/90, and three concrete gaps are named (uninterruptible height animation, dead hover transform, message-skipping double dismiss). Tie-first requires ZERO named gaps. Verdict: fail.
